sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Stephens County?
sections.html:
Two offices carry most of the work, and they sit in different buildings. The Tax Commissioner bills and collects, from Room 103 at 70 North Alexander Street in Toccoa, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. The phone is (706) 886-4753 and the mailing address is PO Box 187, Toccoa, GA 30577. The county site notes that the Tax Commissioner's website is maintained separately from the county's.

The Tax Assessor handles returns, values and homestead applications, and its number is (706) 886-7435. The county's funding page adds that in Stephens County the tax assessors have been delegated the job of receiving tax returns.

sections.h2: Who pays which millage rates in Stephens County?
sections.html:
Every property owner in the county pays the Georgia millage, the Stephens County millage and the Stephens County School System millage. Residents inside Toccoa city limits also pay the Toccoa city millage, so a Toccoa house carries one more layer than a rural parcel with a Toccoa mailing address.

Georgia assesses property at 40 percent of fair market value, and the county notes that one mill equals $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set the rates. If your address could be either city or county, ask the Tax Assessor which digest holds your parcel.

sections.h2: What are the Stephens County deadlines for returns, homestead and appeals?
sections.html:
Stephens County property tax dates and rules, from the county's Tax Assessor and Tax Commissioner pages
ItemRule
Owner for tax purposesThe owner on January 1
Property tax return filingJanuary 1 through April 1, with the Tax Assessor
Homestead exemption for the current yearApplication by April 1; later applications apply to the next year
Real estate and business personal property billsGenerally due November 15
Appeal of an assessment noticeReceived within 45 days of the notice date
Penalty for not filing a required return10% of the value not returned, plus interest
Refund request for erroneous taxWritten claim within 3 years of payment

Refunds cover errors of fault and not disagreements about value, according to the Tax Commissioner's website. An appeal that the Board of Tax Assessors does not resolve goes to the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions can Stephens County owners claim?
sections.html:
The county lists these exemptions on its homestead page, with the state code section for each:

  • A standard $2,000 exemption for a primary residence, deducted from the 40% assessed value, for state, county and school taxes other than school taxes levied by municipalities.
  • A senior exemption at 65 and older, plus a second one when net income for the person and spouse stays at or under $10,000.
  • An age 62 school exemption on the same $10,000 net income test, capped at $10,000 of assessed value.
  • A floating inflation-proof exemption for owners 62 and older, with household income at or under $30,000.
  • A $50,000 exemption for qualifying disabled veterans, which can pass to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.

Owners must own and occupy the home on January 1. The county adds that once granted, an exemption renews automatically unless ownership changes, so a buyer files a new application. A deferral program lets owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less defer tax until ownership changes or the deferred amount reaches 85% of fair market value. The state's Homeowners Tax Relief Grant was withdrawn in 2008.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Stephens County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 27,854 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.0% from the April 2020 base of 26,780, with 12,461 housing units. For 2020 to 2024, the owner-occupied rate is 73.6%, the median owner-occupied home value is $175,300 and median gross rent is $820. Median household income is $54,754, and 23.3% of residents are 65 or older.

The county covers 178.86 square miles of land at about 150 people per square mile, so most parcels are not in a compact city grid. The Census Bureau counts 36 building permits for 2025 against the 12,461 units already standing. Toccoa holds the Historic Courthouse at 37 West Tugalo Street, where the board of elections also works.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Stephens County?
sections.html:
The county's property deeds page lists the figures it uses: a transfer tax of $1 for every $1,000 of money paid, with fifty cents of that tax going to the county for each deed recorded and the rest to the state, a $25 filing fee, a $5 blank deed form and 50 cents a page for copies. The grantor's signature must be witnessed and notarized, and the clerk can help calculate what is due.

Warranty deeds must carry a transfer tax form whether or not money changes hands, and the forms can be completed online at the state clerks' authority site. Filing a deed is not required for it to be legal, but the county says filing protects the owner. A closing attorney usually prepares the deed.

sections.h2: How do I pay or find a Stephens County tax bill?
sections.html:
The county site has an Online Payments page, and the Tax Assessor's page links to an online tax record search and a tax estimator. The Tax Commissioner's separate website lists the main office hours and numbers given above.

The county charges property tax to the owner as of January 1, so a seller who closes later in the year should ask how the year's bill will be handled. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the balance on your parcel before you sign a contract, then settle any amount owed at closing through your attorney. A house with unpaid tax can be levied upon and eventually sold, per the Tax Commissioner's website.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Stephens County, GA?
faqs.a: Generally November 15 for real estate and business personal property, according to the Tax Commissioner's website. Confirm the date printed on your own bill with the office at (706) 886-4753.

faqs.q: What is the Stephens County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. An application received after April 1 is activated the following year. You must own and occupy the home as of January 1, and the application goes to the Tax Assessor's office.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Stephens County assessment?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. The Tax Assessor's page says appeals must be received within that window, and the Tax Commissioner's website says unresolved appeals go to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Do Toccoa residents pay extra property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Residents inside Toccoa city limits pay the Toccoa city millage in addition to the Georgia, Stephens County and Stephens County School System millage.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax when a Stephens County house sells?
faqs.a: The county's deeds page prints $1 for every $1,000 of money paid. Fifty cents of the tax goes to the county for each deed recorded, and the rest goes to the state. Ask the Clerk of Court to confirm the amount for your sale.
